html:
Germany's political landscape is being significantly reshaped after the far-right AfD achieved a historic electoral victory in a key state, prompting the party to assert that "democracy demands" other parties work with them to form a government. This development is described as shaking Germany and Europe to its core, highlighting a broader rise in nationalist and anti-migrant sentiment across the continent.

US Diplomacy: Top US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have traveled to Kyiv for the first time, following talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow, in an effort to restart peace talks between Russia and Ukraine, though reports indicate no breakthrough has been achieved. Separately, Secretary of State Marco Rubio is visiting three Latin American countries as President Trump hails a shift to the right in regional politics and a new era of US dominance. Domestically, advocacy groups comprising veteran lawyers are expanding legal challenges against Trump’s executive orders on voting and other presidential actions, condemning what they describe as a "full-out assault on democracy."

Middle East Security: The conflict between Israel and Lebanon has escalated significantly, with Israeli strikes in southern Lebanese villages killing at least 12 people and destroying a hospital, which Lebanon claims jeopardizes a US-brokered ceasefire. This follows reports of a Palestinian child killed in Gaza and Palestinian parents fearing for their children's lives in the occupied West Bank amidst growing settler attacks. In a shift in foreign policy, Ed Miliband announced the UK will adopt a tougher stance on Israel, imposing a ban on trade in goods and some services from illegal Israeli settlements, a move expected to draw fierce criticism from the US and Israel. Nicaragua is also challenging German arms exports to Israel at the International Court of Justice.

Global Economy: Oil prices remain near $97, driven by a geopolitical premium linked to the US-Iran conflict and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, where shipping traffic has fallen significantly despite US assertions that the waterway is fully open. Iran's economy faces increasing pressure, with gasoline prices doubled and US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stating that Iran has only about 30 million barrels of oil left for China due to US sanctions and a naval blockade. Amidst these tensions, Trump has threatened to block Canada’s Bombardier sales in the United States unless the planes are manufactured there, accusing Canada of unfair practices.

European Tensions: Across Europe, the rise of far-right movements is intertwined with social unrest and historical grievances. Thousands gathered in Serbia for the funeral of Ratko Mladić, the "Butcher of Bosnia" convicted of genocide, leading the EU to issue a warning against the glorification of war criminals. In the UK, police used batons and pepper spray to repel hundreds of masked, black-clad vigilantes during anti-migrant protests in Portsmouth, with the policing minister condemning the "intimidating and thuggish" aggression.

Global Events: Major international incidents include an Amazon cargo jet crash at Miami international airport that killed five people and injured five others, and an Indonesian volcano eruption that has left 340,000 stranded as airports extend closures. In Russia's North Caucasus, an avalanche killed at least 11 climbers. On the humanitarian front, the UN passed a resolution ahead of the General Assembly calling for an end to child marriage, noting an estimated 650 million women and girls globally were married before age 18.
